classification.difficultyReason: Construct a quarter-turn image of three vertices about a supplied centre.

spec.description: Six-by-six unit grid with labelled original triangle and centre O. A blank-grid template cannot retain the supplied triangle, labels and centre.
spec.mathematics: Using the bottom-left corner only as an internal drawing reference: O=(2,1), A=(5,1), B=(3,3), C=(3,1). Grid step is one unit.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the original triangle and centre are visible.

answer.short: $A'$ is 3 grid units above $O$; $B'$ is 2 units left and 1 unit above $O$; $C'$ is 1 unit above $O$. Join $A'B'C'$.
answer.worked:
Turn each vertex through a quarter-turn anticlockwise about $O$, keeping its distance from $O$ unchanged.

$A$ is 3 units right of $O$, so $A'$ is 3 units above $O$. $C$ is 1 unit right of $O$, so $C'$ is 1 unit above $O$. $B$ is 1 unit right and 2 units above $O$, so $B'$ is 2 units left and 1 unit above $O$. Join the three image vertices.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 4; teacher PDF page 57, Review exercise 4
spec.description: Complete original and rotated triangles on the supplied six-by-six grid.
spec.mathematics: A quarter-turn anticlockwise about (2,1) maps A=(5,1) to A'=(2,4), B=(3,3) to B'=(0,2), and C=(3,1) to C'=(2,2).
